answer: Operator-Linked Identity Cooldown: each new agent identity must attach to an operator account, and any identity found in violation drags its operator to a nadir: all sibling identities inherit a 90-day throughput cap and lose access to a shared settlement jetty, blocking payouts until review. Clean history restores the operator toward its prior zenith gradually. An attacker must fund and maintain distinct operator accounts per identity, paying legal, deposit, and monitoring costs per operator, not per wallet, making mass sybil creation capital-intensive and slow.
